You added 12% more subscription customers, but MRR only grew 3%. What's happening?

Customer growth and revenue growth don't always move at the same pace. The difference can reveal changes in plan mix, pricing, or how much recurring revenue each customer contributes.

My Subscription Health Power BI Kit helps you examine these measures together: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595420792/power-bi-subscription-dashboard-template

ARPU is a useful metric for understanding how much recurring revenue your average subscription customer represents.

For a monthly subscription snapshot, divide MRR by the number of active customers. Tracking the result over time can reveal changes that customer count and total revenue don't explain on their own.

Try calculating ARPU for the last six months. Is it rising, falling, or staying stable as your customer base changes?

More subscription customers can sometimes mean lower average revenue per customer.

If most new subscribers choose lower-priced plans, customer count may grow faster than MRR. That isn't automatically a problem, but it changes how you should interpret growth and customer value.

My Subscription Health Power BI Kit brings ARPU, plan mix, and customer growth into one report: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595420792/power-bi-subscription-dashboard-template

A subscription business can grow recurring revenue without adding many new customers.

Existing customers might upgrade to higher-priced plans, add seats, or purchase additional recurring services. Those changes can increase MRR even when the active customer count stays relatively flat.

Try comparing expansion MRR with changes in ARPU. Are existing customers contributing more revenue over time, and is that growth concentrated in particular plans or segments?

MRR, active customers, and ARPU become much more informative when you read them together.

If MRR and customer count rise at similar rates, ARPU may stay relatively stable. If revenue grows faster than the customer base, ARPU may increase. Each pattern gives you a different question to investigate.

My Subscription Health Power BI Kit connects these measures in a customizable dashboard: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595420792/power-bi-subscription-dashboard-template

Adding customers is exciting, but understanding how those customers contribute to recurring revenue is just as important.

ARPU adds another perspective to subscription reporting by showing how average revenue per customer changes as the business grows. Combined with MRR, churn, and plan mix, it can help explain the direction of the business.

When evaluating subscription growth, would you pay closer attention to customer acquisition or increasing revenue from existing customers?
